method: First 15 rows of ~/codewatch-research/gaps/misses.tsv (rows 2-16, all cve-pairs-python, taken in file order). For each case the fix commit was fetched with gh api repos/O/R/commits/SHA (per-file patches) and, where the patch did not show the vulnerable side, the files at the fix commit's parent with gh api contents?ref=SHA^ (validate.py, api/v1/validate.py, file_store.py, server/handlers.py, editor.py, utils.py, lektor/admin/modules/api.py, lektor/db.py, views/article.py, templatetags/wiki_tags.py, includes/searchresult.html, endpoints.py, resolverapi/__init__.py, helpers.py, app_blueprint.py, templates/login.html, routers/terminals.py, postgres/utils.py, postgres/base.py, postgres/queryparser.py, workflows/views.py, common/_workflow.html, views/auth_forms.py, stacks/forms.py, common/_form_field.html, upload/handlers/common/vector.py, servers/main.py, servers/dependencies.py, utils/urls.py). All API calls were one at a time with 2 s between. Nothing was skipped: every row yielded a note. Notes describe the vulnerable side (the fix's parent) and the line numbers in it. GHSA-h3h4-3r2q-9m76 is unsure because the repo has no template or other code that turns the Flask-RESTful abort message into HTML, so the reflected-XSS rendering the advisory names is not visible in the repository.

notes.probe:
import os
from flask import Flask, request

app = Flask(__name__)
ROOT = "/tmp/mlruns"

@app.post("/traces")
def start_trace():
    trace_id = request.json["trace"]["trace_id"]
    d = os.path.join(ROOT, "traces", trace_id)
    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    with open(os.path.join(d, "trace.yaml"), "w") as f:
        f.write("x")
    return {"ok": True}

notes.probe:
import urllib.parse
import websockets
from fastapi import FastAPI, WebSocket

app = FastAPI()

@app.websocket("/terminals/{session_id}")
async def ws_terminal(websocket: WebSocket, session_id: str, policy_id: str | None = None):
    await websocket.accept()
    base = "ws://terminal:8000"
    if policy_id:
        url = f"{base}/p/{policy_id}/api/terminals/{session_id}"
    else:
        url = f"{base}/api/terminals/{session_id}"
    url += "?" + urllib.parse.urlencode({"user_id": "me"})
    async with websockets.connect(url) as upstream:
        await upstream.send(await websocket.receive_text())

import subprocess
from django.http import JsonResponse

def create_ogr2ogr_command(files, original_name, alternate):
    input_file = files["temp_vrt_file"]
    options = f'"{input_file}" -lco FID=ogc_fid '
    options += f'-nln {alternate} "{original_name}"'
    return options

def import_layer(request):
    options = create_ogr2ogr_command(request.FILES, request.POST["name"], request.POST["alternate"])
    subprocess.Popen("ogr2ogr " + options, shell=True)
    return JsonResponse({"ok": True})
